title: OpenAI adds cheaper model to Dots as compute costs mount
summary: The ChatGPT maker's consumer chief called its Pro-only personal assistants "compute heavy," echoing Musk's warning that Grok Bot costs are unsustainable.
bullets:
- **OpenAI** said Tuesday it added the smaller **GPT-6.1 Terra** model to power Dots, letting assistants route some tasks away from the costlier GPT-6 Astra.
- ChatGPT consumer head **Adam Fry** called Dots "compute heavy," noting each runs its own cloud computer and remains limited to the $100-a-month Pro plan.
- **Elon Musk** called Grok Bot's costs "unsustainably high," while OpenAI has raised less than half its $30 billion target, per The Wall Street Journal.

sections.heading: OpenAI Dots compute costs raise doubts on personal AI agents
sections.body:
OpenAI says its new Dots personal assistants use a lot of computing power. The company is now sending some of their work to a smaller, cheaper model. The admission adds to doubts about whether the industry can afford always-on AI agents. At a dinner with reporters in New York on Monday, November 2, Adam Fry, head of ChatGPT's consumer business, said Dots are "on the compute heavy side." He added that each assistant runs its own cloud computer to carry out tasks for users across their connected accounts.

Rivals face the same problem. Elon Musk said this week that the cost of running Grok Bot, the personal assistant SpaceX launched in August, is "unsustainably high relative to revenue." He suggested the company was cutting back the computing power assigned to it, so users hit their limits sooner. The industry's push into agents follows the success of Meta's Muse assistant, according to Fortune.

sections.heading: A cheaper model in the mix
sections.body:
On Tuesday, November 3, OpenAI said it was expanding the models that power dots to include GPT-6.1 Terra. A dot can now use different models for different parts of its work. Terra is smaller and needs less computing power than GPT-6 Astra, which originally ran every Dots task. The new automatic router is meant to make Dots less compute-intensive.

For now, Dots are only available on the $100-a-month Pro plan. Fry said bringing them to more users depends on a breakthrough in compute efficiency, which he expects will come and drive costs down quickly. He also wants Dots to become an always-available presence through features like "background mode," which would mean using even more compute.

sections.heading: Funding gets harder
sections.body: Money is the other constraint. OpenAI has secured about $11 billion in commitments for its latest round, less than half of its $30 billion target, at a $1.25 trillion valuation, The Wall Street Journal reported. The company had hoped for $1.4 trillion. The Financial Times reported that OpenAI cut its goal to $20 billion, with a later offering for wealthy individuals meant to close the gap. OpenAI has not publicly confirmed the figures.

sections.heading: Chips and competition
sections.body: OpenAI relies mostly on Nvidia GPUs and plans to scale up production of its in-house chip, called Jalapeno, in 2027, Fortune reported. Anthropic, which uses four types of chips, has signed purchase agreements worth $895.4 billion, "substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure," according to its amended S-1. Even so, it lists the inability to secure more compute as a major risk. Fortune put the problem this way: "the more powerful—and constantly running—personal AI agents become, the more compute they consume. Will OpenAI ever be able to catch up with itself?"

title: Pangram expands AI detection to images and video
summary: Pangram Image 1.0 replaces a July research preview, and a faster Flash model scans video frame by frame, the company says.
bullets:
- **Pangram** released Image 1.0 and the video-focused Image Flash 1.0, saying they scored 99.96% on an internal test and 98.7% on the DF26 benchmark.
- The launch follows a July research preview that came out alongside the Pangram 4 text detector and a $9 million funding round.
- CEO **Max Spero** told Pirate Wires that rival detectors "kind of sucked." He pointed to fake Iran war drone footage and AI images in Amazon ads.

sections.heading: Pangram launches AI image and video detection models
sections.body: Pangram, a startup best known for detecting AI-written text, released Pangram Image 1.0 on Wednesday, Nov. 4. The image model replaces a research preview from earlier this year, and the company also released a companion model built to detect AI-generated video. With the launch, Pangram's product line now covers images and video as well as text. CEO Max Spero said the move responds to AI imagery that is getting harder to spot.

sections.heading: Two new models
sections.body:
The flagship Pangram Image 1.0 produces a heatmap showing where AI content appears in an image. Pangram says it holds up against edits, compression and low resolutions. The company lowered the minimum image size from 512x512 to 256x256 pixels, though results below 512 pixels come with a reduced-confidence disclaimer. Pangram reported 99.96% accuracy on an internal test set of 1,200 synthetic images, made with 12 frontier generators that mirrored 100 real photos.

The second model, Pangram Image Flash 1.0, is a smaller, faster model aimed at video. It analyzes clips frame by frame. Pangram said it scored 98.7% on the DF26 academic benchmark, 29 points ahead of the next-best detector. Both models are now part of Pangram's Chrome extension, which flags AI content on social media, shopping sites and rental listings. They are also available through the company's API.

sections.heading: Why Pangram moved beyond text
sections.body:
Spero told Pirate Wires that the company started work on image detection at the beginning of the year. He pointed to people trying to "create a hoax or create fake Iran war drone footage." He also said detection could be useful on platforms like Amazon, where ads increasingly use AI-generated images. Pangram tested existing detectors first. "We ran our benchmark and found that most of them, they kind of sucked, like 80 to 95% accuracy," Spero said.

The July research preview reported 99.5% accuracy on an internal benchmark, against 98% for the closest of five commercial competitors. At that stage, Pangram said it could not reliably detect deepfakes or face swaps. The preview came out alongside Pangram 4, the company's text detector, and a $9 million funding round led by Menlo Ventures.

sections.heading: Arriving late on purpose
sections.body: Pangram is not first to this market. Competitors such as TruthScan have offered image and video detection since 2025 or earlier. Spero said the delay was deliberate. "We've been very careful with our release cadence to make sure we only release something that we think is truly state-of-the-art by a large margin," he said.

title: WHO backs Moderna, Oxford Ebola vaccines for Congo trial
summary: WHO says the shots will be the first Bundibugyo-specific vaccines tested during an outbreak that has killed over 5,000 in Congo.
bullets:
- **WHO** advisers recommended **Moderna's** Moderna, Inc. mRNA-1469 and **Oxford's** ChAdOx1 for the Tumaini ring-vaccination trial in Congo, pending national approvals.
- **Congo** has reported 10,532 confirmed cases and 5,126 deaths, with community transmission ongoing and no licensed Bundibugyo vaccine, according to the **ECDC**.
- Moderna says early trial data showed a single dose was well tolerated and triggered strong antibodies; WHO expects trial results in early 2027.

sections.heading: WHO panel backs Moderna mRNA-1469 Ebola vaccine for Tumaini trial in Congo
sections.body:
Moderna said on Wednesday, November 4, that WHO advisers have recommended its experimental Bundibugyo ebolavirus vaccine, mRNA-1469, for a Phase 2/3 efficacy study in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The company said early clinical results were encouraging. The World Health Organization said its expert groups also recommended ChAdOx1, a vaccine developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India. Both will join the ongoing Tumaini trial once national approvals come through.

According to WHO, this will be the first time vaccines built specifically against Bundibugyo virus are tested during an outbreak of the disease. WHO expects vaccine trial results in early 2027.

sections.heading: How the trial works
sections.body:
Tumaini tests several vaccine candidates within a single trial. It uses ring vaccination, which means vaccinating the contacts of people with confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease. The method builds on the Guinea trial that showed Ervebo works against Zaire ebolavirus during the West Africa outbreak. WHO said four vaccination rings are already in place and more are being prepared. The DRC's Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale and the University of Antwerp co-sponsor the randomized, blinded study, which is overseen by the DRC Ministry of Health.

Moderna said WHO's Technical Advisory Group on Candidate Vaccine Prioritization reviewed the evidence on October 22. Interim Phase 1 data from healthy adults in Canada showed the shot was generally well tolerated, and a single dose produced strong antibody responses against Bundibugyo virus. The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) has committed up to $58.5 million to support the program. "We now have an opportunity to evaluate whether our investigational vaccine can help protect people," said Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel.

sections.heading: An outbreak still spreading
sections.body:
No licensed vaccine exists specifically for Bundibugyo virus disease. As of November 2, the DRC had reported 10,532 confirmed cases and 5,126 deaths across eight provinces since the outbreak began in May, and community transmission is ongoing. Ituri province remains the hardest hit. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention now requires passengers on international flights to the United States to attest that they have not been in the DRC in the previous 21 days.

Research on treatments is also moving forward. The PARTNERS trial, launched in July, is testing the monoclonal antibody MBP134, the antiviral remdesivir, or both together, and maftivimab will soon be added. WHO expects early findings from the treatment trials in the coming months.

"Vaccines alone will not end this outbreak, but they could become a powerful new tool for bringing it under control," said WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.

title: PS5 Exclusive God of War Laufey Has Officially Been Delayed by Three Months - Push Square
text:
Developer Santa Monica Studio has just announced its upcoming game, God of War Laufey , has been delayed.

Originally planned for release on 16th February 2027, the PS5 exclusive action game will now launch just over three months later on 20th May.

"Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we've been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye's journey through the Everywhen," the statement says. "We don't take for granted the trust placed in our studio to make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication of our fans."

Santa Monica Studio says it'll "make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential."

God of War Laufey is the next entry in Sony's popular action series, chronicling the journey of Kratos' late wife, Faye, as she navigates the afterlife.

As mentioned in the above statement, the game was officially announced in June of this year, and even then it appeared to be close to release. At the time, some thought Sony was pushing Laufey harder than the imminent Marvel's Wolverine .

Still, the game will launch within a year of its announcement, which is pretty good going.

title: Voters back dozens of data center bans in midterms
summary: At least 33 local measures restricting data centers passed or led Wednesday, as Ohio drove the wave; just one backed construction.
bullets:
- In the Nov. 3 midterms, voters approved bans, moratoriums and limits on data centers in at least 33 communities, according to Capacity.
- In **Ohio**, at least 14 municipalities passed bans or restrictions, including a Trenton measure blocking a proposed Amazon Amazon.com, Inc. campus, Fortune reported.
- Goldman Sachs The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. economists warned moratoriums could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion, per Business Standard.

sections.heading: Voters approve dozens of local data center bans in midterm elections
sections.body: Voters around the country backed bans, moratoriums and other limits on data centers in the November 3 midterm elections. By Wednesday morning, 33 ballot measures restricting data center development had passed or were leading, according to the tracker Data Centers on the Ballot. Only one measure, in Harwood, North Dakota, went in favor of construction, and several races were still being counted. The local results came alongside wins for Democratic candidates who promised tighter rules on data centers. Analysts say that combination could slow the AI infrastructure buildout.

sections.heading: Ohio leads the wave
sections.body:
Ohio held more than half of the 41 data center measures that Ballotpedia counted nationwide. Voters in 18 Ohio municipalities decided 21 measures, and at least 14 municipalities passed bans or other restrictions. In Trenton, a ban on data centers larger than 25 megawatts passed with about 80% of the vote. The ban blocks the city's plan to annex land for a proposed 1,000-megawatt Amazon campus. In Ashville, about 82% of voters rejected a deal with developer EdgeConneX.

The results reached well beyond Ohio. About 77% of voters in Edgewater, Florida, approved a ban, and 82% in Alhambra, California, supported one. Bloomington, Illinois, and the Maine towns of Peru and Wiscasset approved moratoriums. A pause in Emporia, Kansas, was leading with 60% in early returns. In an NBC News exit poll, 76% of voters said they would oppose a new data center in their community.

sections.heading: Governors promising tougher rules
sections.body: Democrats won governor's races in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, states that Republicans had long controlled. In Texas, Gina Hinojosa defeated Gov. Greg Abbott after promising to pause data center approvals right away. Ohio's Amy Acton has called for a "conditional moratorium," and Georgia's Keisha Lance Bottoms has backed a statewide pause. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds, a supporter of data center construction, won the governorship.

sections.heading: Concerns for the AI buildout
sections.body:
Goldman Sachs economists warned that short-term moratoriums could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion. Some analysts were more cautious. "Even if statewide moratoria do not result, we expect to see a lot more sand in the gears of the AI buildout," said Libby Cantrill of PIMCO. Some of the local measures are nonbinding and could face legal challenges.

"Voters had their say tonight," Republican strategist Brendan Steinhauser told Time. He predicted "a big deluge of bills at the state and federal level" aimed at the AI industry.

title: ‘The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’ Remake Metacritic Review Score Is Historic - Forbes
summary: Nintendo's new Ocarina of Time remake enshrines its place in the gaming canon for generations to come. But despite its stupendous production values, the game left me feeling oddly bereft.
text:
Link, the Hero of Time, grown-up and newly awoken from a magical seven-year slumber. Nintendo hide caption

With its tale of an idyllic world despoiled by the lust for power, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time feels as relevant today as it did in 1998. Nintendo's new remake, out Thursday on the Switch 2, enshrines its place in the gaming canon for generations to come. But despite its stupendous production values and painstaking details, the game left me feeling oddly bereft.

Perhaps I should have expected as much. Ocarina of Time weaponizes nostalgia even within its narrative, as the protagonist Link ventures to save his post-apocalyptic world as an adult after first working through it as a kid. You'll uncover old characters enduring new catastrophes. You'll try to rescue everyone you meet. You'll strive to bring things back to how they were before — no, better than they were before.

Seven years stretch between Link's childhood and adult adventures. 28 years yawn between the remake and the original's release. Both in and out of the game, Ocarina of Time makes us yearn for an idealized past.

Decent remakes evoke how you remember a game rather than re-create dated controls and chunky graphics. In myriad small ways, Nintendo has brought Ocarina of Time up to contemporary standards while (mostly) preserving its soul.

In one of the game's most poignant scenes, kid Link answers to the call to adventure, leaving his friend Saria and the Kokiri Forest they called home. Nintendo

title: French blood service says hackers tampered with freezers
summary: Hackers raised cold-room temperature settings at three sites through a contractor's system; no blood products were lost, the agency says.
bullets:
- France's blood service **EFS** confirmed Wednesday that hackers changed cold-room settings at three sites overnight Nov. 1-2 through a contractor's system, Le Monde reported.
- Rooms normally kept at -30°C were programmed to reach 110°C, but alarms caught it, and **EFS** says no blood products were lost.
- Supplier **Coolworld** blamed third-party software, per Politico Europe; the attack follows supermarket fridge hacks across Europe that many officials link to **Moscow**.

sections.heading: Cyberattack targets French blood bank cold stores
sections.body:
Hackers remotely changed the settings on cold rooms holding donated blood products at three sites run by France's national blood service. It is the latest in a string of attacks on refrigeration systems that has worried officials across Europe. The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said a "cybersecurity incident" at one of its refrigeration contractors on Monday, November 2, hit the monitoring and control systems at the three sites, according to AFP.

The EFS said no blood products were lost and patients were not affected. Still, the incident shows how hacking a single supplier's software can reach critical health infrastructure.

sections.heading: Settings raised to 110°C
sections.body:
The EFS said in a statement that "temperature and defrosting thresholds were raised to very high temperatures" in cold rooms that use the provider's system, Le Monde reported. The rooms stored plasma bags meant for transfusions and for making medicines, franceinfo reported. The French weekly Le Canard enchaîné first reported the breach. It said rooms normally kept at -30°C were set to reach 110°C, according to Sud Ouest. The EFS said the rooms never reached that temperature. A technician on duty spotted the problem overnight and stepped in, Euronews reported.

"Our alarm and monitoring systems allowed us to spot very quickly that the settings had been changed," EFS president Frédéric Pacoud told franceinfo. The affected products were moved to other facilities as a precaution, and blood collection and distribution carried on as usual, Le Parisien reported. France's health minister said there had been "no impact on public health," according to la Repubblica.

sections.heading: Contractor points to third-party software
sections.body: French media named the contractor as Coolworld, a refrigeration company. Coolworld said the breach "concerns a component supplied by a third-party provider and not directly controlled by Coolworld" and that only a "limited number" of its units were affected, Politico Europe reported. The health minister's office said technical investigations are still under way. They aim to establish how the attack was carried out, how many machines may be involved and when the affected units can be brought back into service, according to Sud Ouest.

sections.heading: Pattern of fridge attacks
sections.body:
The blood bank breach follows an October 12 attack that disrupted refrigeration at hundreds of supermarkets, Les Dernières Nouvelles d'Alsace reported. Since then, a new wave of attacks on supermarket fridges across Europe has forced stores to throw out spoiled food. Officials have not said who is behind the attacks, though many are looking to Moscow, Politico Europe reported.

Speaking in the Senate, French Digital Minister Anne Le Hénanff said the attacks "have directly targeted our economy and our supply chain." She added that their aim "may potentially be to undermine the unity of our country and to create anxiety among the population," Politico Europe reported.

title: Qualcomm to supply 5G gear for SpaceX's Starlink Mobile
summary: Qualcomm calls the multi-year agreement its biggest 5G deal yet, with equipment headed to tens of thousands of cell sites starting 2027.
bullets:
- **Qualcomm** Qualcomm Incorporated will supply radios, baseband units and software for **Starlink Mobile's** planned nationwide US 5G network, without disclosing terms, Reuters reported.
- **SpaceX** holds about 80MHz of spectrum versus T-Mobile's T-Mobile US, Inc. roughly 400MHz; Omdia analyst Gabriel Brown says massive MIMO can "bridge some of the gap".
- The deal pits Qualcomm against **Marvell** Marvell Technology, Inc., **Broadcom** Broadcom Inc. and **Intel** Intel Corporation in tower chips, while SpaceX bypasses **Ericsson** Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson and **Nokia** Nokia Oyj.

sections.heading: Qualcomm signs multi-year 5G deal with SpaceX for Starlink Mobile
sections.body: Qualcomm said on Wednesday, November 4, that it has signed a multi-year agreement with SpaceX. Under the deal, Qualcomm will supply radio equipment, baseband units and software for Starlink Mobile's planned nationwide terrestrial 5G network in the US. Qualcomm did not disclose financial terms but called it "our biggest 5G deal yet," Reuters reported. The equipment is set to go into tens of thousands of macro cell sites starting in 2027. The contract gives the smartphone chipmaker a larger role in telecom infrastructure. It also backs SpaceX's push to compete with AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile.

sections.heading: What Qualcomm is supplying
sections.body:
SpaceX chose Qualcomm's Dragonwing QRU100 and QDU100 platforms and its commercial-grade Layer 1 software, according to Qualcomm's announcement. The network will use Massive MIMO radio units with 64 transmit and 64 receive paths, a design meant to improve coverage, capacity and spectral efficiency. "Starlink is building the first fully-integrated nationwide satellite and terrestrial network that will keep people connected no matter where they are," Starlink Senior Vice President Michael Nicolls said in the release.

Speaking to reporters, Qualcomm executive Durga Malladi said the agreement is the company's biggest network deal since the 3G era. "This is huge," he said, as quoted by Light Reading. He said Qualcomm has brought 64T64R radios to lower bands "all the way down to 2GHz." SpaceX will build its own Layer 2 and Layer 3 software on top of Qualcomm's foundation. Malladi said the deployment will "ramp up pretty rapidly" once it starts next year.

sections.heading: Spectrum gap and competition
sections.body:
SpaceX's main constraint is spectrum. Through purchases from EchoStar and Grain Management, the company holds roughly 80MHz, compared with about 400MHz for T-Mobile, Light Reading noted. Omdia analyst Gabriel Brown said this kind of massive MIMO is a way to "bridge some of the gap." The announcement came days after reports that SpaceX was talking with US tower owners about access to up to 80,000 sites.

Questions remain about whether SpaceX can make its plans work, given the investment needed to take on the three big carriers, Reuters said. Even so, the company has kept buying spectrum and exploring tower deals.

sections.heading: Shake-up for equipment vendors
sections.body: The deal also brings Qualcomm into competition with Marvell, Broadcom and Intel in cell tower chips, according to Reuters. Qualcomm already helps power 5G networks in Japan and Vietnam. SpaceX appears to have bypassed the traditional network vendors, including Ericsson and Nokia, Light Reading reported. The outlet also pointed to Dish and Rakuten as examples of how hard it is to break into mobile by building a new network from scratch.

title: ChatGPT gave voting info over 16 million times in midterms
summary: OpenAI's Election Operations Center, staffed to catch ChatGPT misuse like deepfakes and influence campaigns, will stay open until all votes are counted.
bullets:
- **ChatGPT** pulled voting data from nonprofit **Democracy Works** more than 16.5 million times this cycle as of Tuesday afternoon, OpenAI told The Hill Nexstar Media Group, Inc..
- The center opened Oct. 29 in **San Francisco** with a Washington satellite office, and it reviews flagged prompts and alerts other platforms, per The New York Times The New York Times Company.
- **Anthropic** and **Meta** Meta Platforms, Inc. also run war rooms as social platforms cut trust and safety teams and the Trump administration dismantled federal anti-interference units.

sections.heading: OpenAI Runs Election War Room as ChatGPT Fields Midterm Voting Questions
sections.body:
OpenAI ran an "Election Operations Center" through the Nov. 3 midterm elections to catch misuse of ChatGPT. The center will stay open until all votes are counted. ChatGPT also pulled voting information from the nonprofit Democracy Works more than 16.5 million times this cycle, according to figures OpenAI gave The Hill as of Tuesday afternoon. That count was expected to rise as Election Day went on.

The effort shows AI companies taking on a monitoring role that social media platforms once led. This comes as tools that can make realistic text, images and video spread quickly.

sections.heading: Inside the operations center
sections.body:
Politico first reported the center on Oct. 28. It said staff from several teams, numbering in the hundreds, would review cases flagged for possible abuse. The work is led by Josh Lawson, OpenAI's head of civic and strategic risk. "The Elections Operations Center builds on that yearslong work, bringing our teams together to respond quickly to emerging issues and enforce our policies as people head to the polls," Lawson told Politico.

The New York Times reported that the center opened on Thursday, Oct. 29. More than a dozen people work around the clock in a San Francisco conference room, with a satellite center in Washington. The team reviews prompts that were automatically flagged as attempts to create false election content, such as plans for influence campaigns using fake accounts. OpenAI alerts other platforms when it finds activity aimed at their sites. "We're not just monitoring text anymore," Lawson told the Times, pointing to threats like deepfakes and cyberattacks. OpenAI's image tools also turn requests for realistic fake scenes, such as long lines at polling places, into cartoons, Action News Jax reported, citing Lawson.

sections.heading: Voter information and results
sections.body: This is OpenAI's first election working with Democracy Works. The nonprofit compiles registration deadlines, ID requirements and polling locations from election offices, The Hill reported. Lawson said that in 2024 the model would often refuse to answer these questions or send users to a website that took several clicks to reach the answer. ChatGPT is relying on The Associated Press to call races, according to Action News Jax.

sections.heading: A broader industry push
sections.body:
Anthropic also set up its own war room for the first time, according to The Hill. Meta opened one again last week, the Times reported. The Times added that social media platforms have scaled back their trust and safety teams in recent years, while the Trump administration has taken apart federal teams that worked against election interference.

In October, OpenAI said it had shut down influence operations tied to Russia and Iran. The company has not disclosed any specific efforts targeting the midterms. "We've been trying to catch operations," OpenAI chief investigator Ben Nimmo told the Times, "before they have a chance to gain traction."

title: China's tech giants expect just 1% of Nvidia chip orders
summary: Buyers including Alibaba and Tencent ordered 6 million RTX Pro 5500 chips but expect tens of thousands within four months, Bloomberg reports.
bullets:
- **Nvidia** NVIDIA Corporation customers in China, including **Alibaba** Alibaba Group Holding Limited and **Tencent** Tencent Holdings Limited, expect about 1% of roughly $70 billion in RTX Pro 5500 orders soon, Bloomberg reported.
- In October, Reuters reported Nvidia warned partners they might get only 5% to 10% of requests, as it shifts **TSMC** Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited capacity toward Rubin chips.
- The workstation chip is among the most powerful Chinese buyers can legally obtain under US export controls, and Beijing signaled it would approve purchases.

sections.heading: Chinese Tech Giants Expect Just 1% of Ordered Nvidia RTX Chips
sections.body:
Chinese AI developers, among them Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance, have ordered about 6 million of Nvidia's RTX Pro 5500 chips. Over the next four months they expect to get only some tens of thousands, roughly 1% of the total, Bloomberg reported on November 4, citing people familiar with the matter. The shortfall comes as the US chipmaker struggles to raise production fast enough to keep up with demand.

Bloomberg valued the orders at about $70 billion, with each chip priced above $11,000. Buyers expect several thousand units by the end of 2026 and tens of thousands more around February, according to Finimize's summary of the report. Some Chinese customers estimate that cumulative deliveries could reach about 700,000 units by the end of 2027. That is roughly 12% of what they ordered. Nvidia told Bloomberg that supply would remain limited for the foreseeable future because of production constraints and scheduling conflicts.

sections.heading: A Squeeze Tighter Than First Signaled
sections.body:
The new timeline is worse than what Nvidia's customers heard in October. On October 20, Reuters reported that ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent alone had ordered more than 3 million RTX Pro 5500 cards at about $11,400 each, worth more than $35 billion combined, and that total orders from China had passed 6 million. One source told Reuters that Nvidia warned partners they might receive only 5% to 10% of what they requested. Another said the company could make no more than 3 million of the cards worldwide in 2027.

Reuters' sources said the cap reflects Nvidia's manufacturing priorities. The company plans to devote much of its capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing to Rubin, its next-generation data-center platform, starting in 2027, according to Reuters' Japanese-language report. Nvidia had told customers to expect early samples in December, with commercial deliveries starting in the first quarter of 2027.

sections.heading: Why China Wants a Workstation Chip
sections.body:
The RTX Pro 5500 is built for powerful professional workstations, not large data-center clusters. Even so, it is among the most powerful Nvidia chips Chinese buyers can still get under US export controls, Reuters noted. Chinese companies plan to use the cards mainly for AI inference, which means running trained models to answer chatbot queries. Inference needs less computing power than training. Washington bars sales of Nvidia's Blackwell B300 to China, and the older H200 needs a case-by-case license, according to Reuters.

Beijing has also signaled it is open to the purchases. In September, China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology asked companies including ByteDance and Alibaba to report their plans to buy the RTX Pro 5500, and told some of them it intended to approve the deals, Reuters reported, citing The Information. The Chinese firms that ordered the chips now face a long wait. In the words of Finimize, access is "being decided by allocation and scheduling, not just price."

title: Xbox Debuts the Series X-BITE: A Working Console Swallowed by an Alligator - Hypebeast

text:
This November, XBOX is heading to Florida – home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe. That felt like the right inspiration for a custom XBOX Series X unlike anything we’ve made before: the XBOX Series X-BITE.

A custom XBOX Wireless Controller with bite marks rests between its jaws, complete with XBOX-green irises and Nexus-inspired pupils, making the XBOX Series X-BITE ready to play some of the biggest games of the year. The result is part-XBOX Series X, part-creature fabrication.

Turning the idea into something real required serious craft.

Creature animatronics specialists John Nolan Studio brought the XBOX Series X-BITE to life through 3D modeling, sculpting and fabrication. The studio has created creatures and animatronics for ‘The Witcher,’ ‘Jurassic World Dominion,’ and HBO’s upcoming ‘Harry Potter’ series.

Every detail was considered, from the texture and finish of the alligator to the custom XBOX Wireless Controller and illuminated console within. At the center of it all is a functioning XBOX Series X.

title: macOS 27.3 adds native Markdown rendering to Quick Look - 9to5Mac
summary: Starting with macOS 27.3, users can preview Markdown files with proper formatting directly in Quick Look. Here are the details.
text:
Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 1 today, with new Safari features, including Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode, expanded Siri AI capabilities, and new tools for third-party developers.

Among the smaller changes coming to the Mac is a welcome improvement to Quick Look. As of macOS 27.3 beta 1, .md files are rendered with proper formatting directly in Quick Look, rather than displaying their raw Markdown syntax.

Apple has been expanding Markdown support across its platforms, including the ability to import and export Markdown files in Notes . Markdown has also become increasingly important with the rise of AI agents, which use .md files to store instructions, context, and other information.

In fact, as Federico Viticci noted today on X , Apple’s new Siri AI app skills feature also uses Markdown-based SKILL.md files, allowing developers to provide instructions that help Siri perform complex tasks within their apps.

For the uninitiated, Markdown is a simple text formatting syntax created by John Gruber in 2004 , and has since become widely used for writing documentation, publishing content online (including this very post), and, more recently, providing instructions to AI agents.

Markdown is a text-to-HTML conversion tool for web writers. Markdown allows you to write using an easy-to-read, easy-to-write plain text format, then convert it to structurally valid HTML.

A revamped voice assistant was one of several new features and design tweaks the company planned to include in its new underlying Sonos 27 software .

When it originally introduced Sonos 27 in September, Sonos said its new voice assistant could be used for "music and mood curation" and mostly focused its attention on its platform's support for third-party AI assistants like ChatGPT and custom agents.

Like the company's previous Voice Control feature , Sonos 27voice can control playback on Sonos devices in your system. It also features basic voice assistant functionality like setting timers, interacting with supported smart home accessories and telling you the current weather. In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.

Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)

Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree.
